query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Employing rapid spark plasma sintering (SPS) with a tailored heating-cooling profile will limit interfacial diffusion during processing, thereby suppressing phase separation and interfacial void formation in a W–Cu composite, which in turn improves its thermal conductivity under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions compared to conventionally processed composites.
generation.material_initial_state: W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix that exhibits significant phase separation and interfacial void formation when processed conventionally.
generation.intervention: Use rapid spark plasma sintering with a tailored heating-cooling profile to minimize diffusion times during sintering.
generation.conditions: Processing under controlled high heating rates and rapid cooling in the SPS process; service conditions mimic those at joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components, including high heat flux and irradiation exposure.
generation.structural_mediator: Suppressed interfacial diffusion between W and Cu, leading to reduced phase separation and decreased formation of voids at the interfaces.
generation.mechanism: The rapid SPS processing reduces the time available for thermal diffusion at the W–Cu interface. This limits the liquid-phase formation that typically leads to phase separation and void nucleation, thus maintaining continuous thermal pathways between phases and enhancing overall thermal conductivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The SPS-treated composite is predicted to exhibit a more homogeneous microstructure with fewer interfacial voids, resulting in a higher thermal conductivity and better resistance to irradiation-induced degradation compared to a composite processed with conventional sintering.
generation.baseline: A W–Cu composite processed conventionally (with slower heating and cooling rates) showing significant interfacial diffusion, phase separation, and void formation, which correlates with lower thermal conductivity under similar operational conditions.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies when the sintering temperature, pressure, and time are optimized to ensure rapid heating and cooling, and when post-processing conditions do not induce additional diffusion. The effect may be limited if the SPS parameters are not tightly controlled or if service conditions exceed the stabilized microstructure's thermal limits.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of thermal conductivity improvement and the quantitative limits of diffusion suppression require experimental validation. Scaling the process and parameter sensitivity could introduce variability that is not fully predictable from current evidence.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two batches of identical W–Cu composite samples. Process one batch using conventional sintering and the other with rapid SPS employing the tailored heating-cooling profile. Subject both sets to controlled heat-transfer cycles and irradiation conditions representative of joint environments. Post-treatment, use scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) to evaluate interfacial microstructure and void formation, and measure their thermal conductivities using standard techniques.
measurements: Interfacial void density and phase homogeneity (via SEM/EDS)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the rapid SPS processed samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in interfacial void formation and non-uniform phase segregation, or if their thermal conductivity under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions is not measurably higher than that of the conventionally processed samples, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: (CrFeTiTa)70W30 and VFeTiTaW alloys were produced by mechanical alloying and sintering and annealed at 1100 °C, 1300 °C, and 1500 °C. The irradiation resistance of the as-sintered materials was also evaluated. Therefore, the materials were irradiated with Ar+ (150 keV) with a fluence of 2.4 × 1020 at/m2, as well as He+ (10 keV) and D+ (5 keV), both with a fluence of 5 × 1021 at/m2. A very fine and homogeneous microstructure composed of three phases was observed in both as-sintered alloys. After annealing, considerable phase growth was observed. Both alloys presented three phases: a phase with a bcc-type structure, a hexagonal C14 Laves phase, and a Ti-rich oxide. These phases maintained their structure even after 8 days at 1500 °C, indicating high thermal stability. It was concluded that for the sample containing Cr, the bcc-type phase is a solid solution of W and Ta, while in the case of the sample containing V, it is a solid solution of W, Ta and V. In both alloys, the Laves phase is derived from Fe2Ta, in which Ta atoms are partially replaced by W atoms and the Fe atoms are partially replaced by Cr or V in the (CrFeTiTa)70W30 alloy and VFeTiTaW alloy, respectively. A powder metallurgical technique using elemental powder mixing has been exploited by developing and analyzing a novel high-entropy alloy (WxTaTiVCr, simplified as xWs) and its derivative alloys for the development of reduced-activation alloys for future fusion power plants. Various compositions realized by varying the W content from 32 to 90at.% with in-situ TiC were prepared by consolidating a powder mixture through spark plasma sintering at 1600 °C. The relative density of the alloys sintered at 1600 °C was found to increase with a decrease in the W content. The characterization of xWs samples by XRD showed the BCC crystal structure of the alloys. A microstructural examination by SEM-EDS revealed multiple phases in the microstructures as bright, gray and dark regions. Moreover, various W-rich phases were observed in the matrix of the sintered samples. An investigation of these phases under TEM and a selected-area diffraction pattern analysis disclosed the presence of TiC in the W-rich matrix, as observed in BSE images. reading.lever: Employ rapid spark plasma sintering with a tailored heating-cooling profile to limit interfacial diffusion.
reading.why: This processing route minimizes diffusion time, thereby suppressing phase separation and void formation, as shown effective in related HEA systems.
